label: Bible Study
prompt: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was _____ unto him for righteousness.
verse: For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
note: Paul reaches back to Genesis 15:6 — Abraham's faith credited as righteousness.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Can a woman forget her sucking _____, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee.
verse: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee.
note: A mother might forget her nursing baby — unthinkable — yet even then, God says, I will not forget thee.

label: Sunday School
prompt: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the _____ of heaven were opened.
verse: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.
note: Modern versions say floodgates; the KJV opens the 'windows of heaven' — the same phrase Malachi later uses for blessing.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I am Alpha and Omega, the _____ and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
verse: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
note: Alpha and Omega are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet — God bookends everything.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a _____, and unto the Greeks foolishness;
verse: But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness;
note: Christ crucified: to some a 'stumblingblock' — one word in the KJV — and to others sheer foolishness.
